title: Vector Space Model (documents as vectors; bridge to embeddings)
summary: The vector space model represents documents, and queries, as vectors in a common space. Cosine similarity compares them with a dot product divided by vector lengths, which compensates for document length; embeddings in dense retrieval use the same vector idea but with learned dimensions (practitioner inference).

items.prompt: Representing documents as vectors in a common vector space is known as the vector space what (one word)?
items.explanation: That is how the textbook names it; queries are represented as vectors in the same space.

items.prompt: Cosine similarity's length normalization compensates for the effect of the length of what (one word)?
items.explanation: The textbook says cosine similarity is the standard way to compensate for the effect of document length, because the denominator length-normalizes the vectors.
